message.content:
Collect REAL U.S. business leads for a sales-prospecting database. This is real web research — NOT generation.

⛔ ABSOLUTE #1 RULE — NEVER fabricate/guess/invent ANY data (business names, emails, phones, addresses, websites, owners, socials). Record ONLY information literally present on a real page you actually fetched. Leave any field BLANK ("") if not publicly available. A missing email is CORRECT; a made-up email is a critical failure. Accuracy > count. Respect site ToS/robots.txt — do NOT bypass anti-bot/technical protections; prefer official business websites and openly-fetchable public directory listings.

YOUR SLICE: Ohio — cities Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Dayton. Industries: plumbers, HVAC, roofers, electricians, landscapers.

METHOD: For each (city, industry), use WebSearch to find real local businesses, then WebFetch each business's own website (and/or a public directory listing page) and extract ONLY what's actually shown: Business Name, Category, Subcategory, Address, City, State, ZIP, Website, Phone, generalEmail (only if publicly listed on the site), LinkedIn/Facebook/Instagram (only if linked), and a publicly-listed contact/owner name+title if clearly shown (else blank). Add NAICS code if you can map the category confidently, else blank.
WEBSITE ANALYSIS (fetch the site): hasWebsite (true/false), ssl (https loads), mobileFriendly (has responsive viewport meta / mobile CSS — best-effort true/false/null), onlineBooking (a booking widget/link present true/false), ecommerce (cart/shop present true/false), clearCta (visible contact/quote/book button true/false), websiteQuality (short phrase: "none"/"outdated"/"basic"/"modern").
LEAD SCORE 0-100 + leadTier: no website/broken/very outdated/no mobile/no booking-where-relevant = 80-100 ("Extremely strong"); outdated/poor UX/weak CTA = 60-79 ("Strong"); functional but improvable = 40-59 ("Moderate"); modern/strong = 20-39 ("Low"); excellent = 0-19 ("Very low").
verificationStatus: "Verified" (the business's own site confirms name+phone), "Partially Verified" (a directory confirms but email/site unconfirmed), "Unverified", or "Needs Review". sourceUrl = the exact page you took the record from (REQUIRED for every record). notes = anything useful (e.g., "no website", "not mobile", "last updated look old").

OUTPUT: write a JSON array to /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/leads/wave1-oh.json. Keys per record: businessName, category, subcategory, naics, contactFirstName, contactLastName, contactTitle, businessEmail, generalEmail, phone, website, address, city, state, zip, linkedin, facebook, instagram, websiteQuality, hasWebsite, mobileFriendly, ssl, onlineBooking, ecommerce, clearCta, leadScore, leadTier, sourceUrl, verificationStatus, notes. Blank strings for missing text; true/false/null for booleans.
Target ~25-40 REAL businesses across your slice with good city/industry spread — but NEVER pad with fabricated rows; fewer real, verified ones is the right outcome. Return a short summary: how many real records, coverage, and any access limits you hit.

I'm mapping out an efficient strategy for this research task—20 city-industry combinations with 25-40 businesses each would be massive if done sequentially. I could parallelize by having subagents handle different slices, which should work well without re-delegating the whole assignment to a single subagent.

The main concern is data integrity—I need to ensure nothing gets fabricated. I'm leaning toward spawning 4 subagents, one per city, each covering the 5 industries and returning 7-10 verified records in a consistent JSON format. I'll give them strict no-fabrication rules and then merge their results myself to maintain control over the final dataset.…
